::: {#hero-heading}
<div class="h1">Welcome</div>

I am a bioinformatics scientist with 25+ years of experience building computational infrastructure for genomics and biomedical research. My expertise spans Bayesian statistics, machine learning, variant calling, and epigenomics. Beyond individual research, I'm committed to mentoring collaborators, developing open-source tools, and modernizing scientific computing through reproducible workflows. I believe accessible, well-designed computational systems amplify the impact of collaborative research.

I'm a Bioinformatics Scientist at the [University of Vermont](https://www.uvm.edu/), Department of Microbiology and Molecular Genetics. Learn more about my work in [publications](/publication).

Get in touch by [sending me a note](/contact.qmd)! {{< fa feather-pointed >}}

:::

## About me

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6 #about-me-1}

**Bioinformatician and data scientist with deep expertise in computational genomics and Bayesian methods.**

I work with R, Python, and workflow management systems like Nextflow to build scalable, reproducible computational pipelines. I'm passionate about effective communication with collaborators and mentor students in bioinformatics methods. My work spans sequence analysis, phylogenetics, epigenomics, and applied machine learning for biomedical research.

<ul class="fa-ul">
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-graduation-cap"></i></span>Ph.D. in Cell and Molecular Biology (Bioinformatics/Statistics) ∙ University of Vermont ∙ 2011</li>
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-graduation-cap"></i></span>B.S. in Pure Mathematics ∙ University of Costa Rica ∙ 1999</li>
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-graduation-cap"></i></span>B.S. in Computer Science ∙ University of Costa Rica ∙ 1999</li>
</ul>

:::

::: {.g-col-6 #about-me-2}

Since 2001, I've worked at the intersection of bioinformatics and collaborative science. I spent ten years in industry as a statistician at a consulting firm while contributing part-time to UVM, gaining expertise in experimental design and rigorous client-facing work. More recently, I lead bioinformatics infrastructure projects, including the development and deployment of Nextflow pipelines through the Seqera platform, and have built web platforms for computational analysis.

I'm deeply interested in artificial intelligence and eager to learn and apply these methods in research. Beyond work, I'm committed to service through meditation and non-violent communication practices.

<ul class="fa-ul">
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-briefcase"></i></span>Bioinformatics Scientist ∙ Vermont Integrative Genomics Resource ∙ UVM ∙ 2022-present</li>
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-briefcase"></i></span>Bioinformatics Scientist ∙ Translational Global Infectious Disease Research ∙ UVM ∙ 2022-present</li>
   <li><span class="fa-li"><i class="fa-solid fa-briefcase"></i></span>Bioinformatics Programmer ∙ University of Vermont ∙ 2001-2006</li>
</ul>

:::
